newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch adj. unemployment shows first rise in a year.
newsitem.headline: Dutch adj. unemployment shows first rise in a year.

text.p: Dutch seasonally adjusted unemployment rose in the April-June period, the first such rise since the June-August period of 1996.
Average seasonally adjusted unemployment for the three months up to and including June came to 395,000, a rise of 10,000 compared with average for the three months to May.
However, the Dutch government's statistics office said it was too early to conclude that the steady decline in Dutch unemployment, under way since early 1994, had come to an end.
The figures did seem to point to a recent slowdown in the rate at which unemployment has been falling, the office added.

The seasonally adjusted April-June jobless total, which represents 5.9 percent of the labour force, was lower than the figure of 438,000 for the same period of 1996 and well below the peak of 503,000 recorded for January-March 1994.

Economists polled by Reuters before publication of the latest figures had predicted a further slight fall in seasonally adjusted unemployment to 383,000 but had noted that the jobless rate was falling less quickly than earlier this year.
